key_insight: A graph neural network can learn an effective magnetic energy functional from electronic calculations and rapidly predict spin torques and dynamics in metallic magnets.
engineering_relevance: This provides a scalable surrogate for expensive electronic simulations, enabling larger and longer nonequilibrium magnetism studies across multiple length and time scales.
method: Train a GNN on electronic-calculation data to represent the magnetic energy functional.
Use the learned functional to evaluate spin torques efficiently during time evolution.
Benchmark on collinear, noncollinear, and noncoplanar metallic magnetic systems.
evidence_signal: The abstract reports that the learned force fields accurately reproduce electronically generated spin torques and match direct electronic-simulation spin dynamics across representative test systems.
watch_item: Performance may depend on the diversity and quality of the electronic training data, especially for extrapolating to new magnetic textures or out-of-distribution dynamics.
paper_title: Graph Neural Network Force Fields for Spin Dynamics in Metallic Magnets
